title: Choose the visual world for TrackAndTrace
question: The roll assigned The Destiny Clock. Keep it, take Railway Mission Control (the pick), Teletext Service, the category standard — or re-roll.

options.label: The Destiny Clock
options.lineage: Indian railway clocks — twin-faced tower clocks over junctions and the platform clock every waiting traveler watches
options.thesis: Railway time decides every ticket; the product is a precision instrument that reads a PNR and shows, on one master clock, whether your seat frees before chart time.
options.viewport: A twin-face master dial fills the stage — left face TIME TO CHART, right face CONFIRMATION ODDS. The PNR entry is engraved beneath the dials; submit sweeps both hands at once, the red second hand racing the chart.
options.risk: A clock motif can read decorative or nostalgic; only instrument-grade restraint and a functionally true red-hand countdown keep it honest.

raised.raise: The odds hand is continuously parametric — live WL movement makes it breathe in real time, never a static needle.
One ruling time axis owns the whole page — the countdown is the composition, never an ornament in a corner.
The full analysis deploys from the compact PNR chip in one gesture: packet to open instrument.
On narrow screens the master dial reflows along the frame instead of stacking into boxes.
Focus reveals detail in place — activating any factor expands it without navigation.

options.label: Railway Mission Control
options.lineage: Indian railway signalling — the green/amber/red aspects every traveler already reads as destiny
options.thesis: Every outcome is a signal aspect; the product is a signal tower where a PNR resolves into one honest light plus the reasoning that earned it.
options.viewport: A control console: the PNR entry sits on an engraved plate; on submit the board resolves through an amber flicker to a solid green/amber/red aspect while a telemetry readout lists each factor's contribution.
options.risk: The direction this category drifts toward — dark console plus status lights — so it must carry the railway's real hardware language to avoid the generic ops-dashboard rut.

options.label: Teletext Service
options.thesis: The PNR is a page number — every ticket is a three-digit address on a live broadcast index.
options.viewport: Keying PNR 302 resolves like a teletext page — status assembles from mosaic blocks while the factors wait behind a REVEAL key.
options.case: Fuses cleanly — readouts, page addresses, and a REVEAL for factor detail are native to it; loses on audience identification with today's Indian traveler.
options.risk: Reads as retro novelty unless the character-cell grid is kept absolutely strict.

options.label: Variable Type Specimen
options.thesis: One giant PNR digit fills the screen and thickens as the odds rise — confidence as a live variable axis.
options.viewport: The ten PNR digits sit in a specimen grid; moving an axis sweeps weight through every glyph while a mono readout counts the value.
options.risk: A typographic conceit that can leave the ticket data feeling like a footnote.
options.kept: Continuous parametric response — one live value morphs the whole instrument.

options.label: Mesophotic Descent
options.thesis: Checking a PNR is a descent toward chart time — the deeper you go the closer the answer, and waitlist is decompression.
options.viewport: A vertical dive profile rules the page; the PNR sits at its current depth between the surface and the chart at turnaround depth.
options.risk: Poetic pressure that can sink the plain data readouts this tool lives on.
options.kept: One ruling vertical axis that every line of the page sits on.

options.label: Miura Deployable
options.thesis: The PNR is a folded packet; one pull deploys the full analysis as a rigid, crease-linked sheet.
options.viewport: A gold chip holds the PNR; tug its corners and the whole analysis unfolds along diagonal seams.
options.risk: The fold metaphor can make routine checking theatrical.
options.kept: Deployment as state — detail unfolds from the compact object in one gesture.

options.label: Gardens Guide Map
options.thesis: The journey is a map of coloured lobes; confirmation lives on one headland that swells to fill the screen.
options.viewport: Each PNR is a lobe on the map; the checked ticket swells until its coast leaves the frame on two sides.
options.risk: Flat-colour map language is the wrong register for a precision data instrument.
options.kept: One continuous composition that reflows along the frame instead of stacking.

options.label: Streaming Title Wall
options.thesis: PNRs as a wall of rails; the tile you land on lifts and tells its story while the room dims behind it.
options.viewport: Watchlist as a wall of ticket tiles — the focused one expands to reveal status, odds, and the next check.
options.risk: Entertainment-catalog pacing is wrong for high-frequency status checking.
options.kept: Progressive disclosure — focus reveals detail in place, without navigation.

canonCard.label: Category standard
canonCard.thesis: The PNR checker this category ships, executed impeccably and honestly — a clean, light utility page.
canonCard.viewport: A light utility page: a large PNR input on top, a status-and-probability card below.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from the competition by design.
